title: Good News, Bad News; Shaw Festival's The Lady From The Sea - Excellent - And
venue: Court House Theatre; Royal George Theatre

display_heading.headline: Good News, Bad News
display_heading.deck: Shaw Festival's The Lady From The Sea - Excellent - And Peter And The Starcatcher - Less So - Offer A Study In Contrasts

contact_edits.before: Act Two features a band of semicannibals whose vocabulary derives entirely from Italian cuisine; and what passes for humour depends entirely on stepping cutely out of context. The only ingenuity comes in the way the story finally dovetails with J. M. Barrie's original; the only emotion piggybacks shamelessly on that same source. In these respects it's like Wicked, but probably worse. Charlie Gallant makes a good impression as Peter. Kate Besworth is the Wendyish young lady who rescues and inspires him; it's a repeat of her performance in Arcadia, which I've certainly no objection to seeing again. The boy discovers leadership but the girl is always ahead of him; we get it already. So did Barrie. Martin Happer is the future Captain Hook, prone to accidents and anachronisms; he gives it a good shot but Ross Petty would do it more natural. A large cast pitches enthusiastically in; Jackie Maxwell's production relies heavily on standardized methods of suggesting waves and storms, and on the supposed outrageousness of Shaw Festival actors dressing up like mermaids (them again) for a musical number. The Broadway reviews made the play sound interesting: fooled again. A plague on all prequels, say I. robert.cushman@hotmail.com
